text:
deploy-bot: :rotating_light: prod deploy started for service-inference v2.4.3 -> includes KMS alias rotation to alias/redwood-prod-key (canary=10%). rollout id: r-2026-03-15-09:12

alex: noticing streaming errors in prod logs, "failed to decrypt env var DB_PASSWORD: AccessDeniedException" on several pods in canary pool

maria: stack-trace snippet from pod inference-canary-12:
```
Error: KMS Decrypt failed: AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:sts::123456789:assumed-role/service-role is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource: alias/redwood-prod-key
at decryptSecrets (/app/startup/secrets.js:42:15)
at processTicksAndRejections (internal/process/task_queues.js:95:5)
```

jen: paging @oncall - we have failing canary decrypts, starting incident triage. api errors at ~1.2% overall but spikes to 8% in regions with canaries.

taylor: I'll take oncall. quick check: did the deploy include IAM change/role propagation? canary used new key alias that may not have updated grants. checking cloudtrail now.

rohan: I see a key-rotation event 09:06 UTC and a deploy job that referenced alias/redwood-prod-key without principal policy update. looks like CI job created new key and the service role wasn't added to key policy.

incident-bot: Incident opened: INC-20260315-047. Severity: P2. Affected: inference-serving (decrypt failures), approx 2000 requests/min with 502s for some clients. Pager escalation sent to oncall and eng-sre.

sam: mitigation options: 1) kill feature flag that swaps to new KMS alias (feature: kms-key-rotation) 2) rollback deploy to previous container image 3) patch key policy to add service role (fast but risky during rotation).

alex: we should kill the flag first to stop new pods from using the alias. command in console or via FF API: 
```
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $FF_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"feature":"kms-key-rotation","enabled":false}' \
  https://console.redwood.dev/api/flags/toggle
```

maria: flipping flag now. I'm hitting endpoint... response 200. turning down canary traffic to 0%.

deploy-bot: Feature flag toggled: kms-key-rotation=false by maria at 4105001240. Canary traffic reduced to 0%.

jen: confirm: are new pods still starting with new alias? need to ensure no requeue of pending pods picks up the new env.

rohan: kube rollout pause? we already stopped rollout; but existing canary pods that failed won't rejoin until restart. I'm applying an env override to point to old alias alias/redwood-prod-key-old as immediate fallback:
```
kubectl set env deployment/inference -n prod KMS_ALIAS=alias/redwood-prod-key-old --record
```

alex: applied override on prod. restarting failing pods. logs show decrypt using old alias now, successful. error rate dropping to baseline.

incident-bot: Incident update: mitigation in place, error rate down to 0.3%. Still monitoring for 30m. Incident severity downgraded to P3 if stable.

sam: next step: we need a safe remediation for rotation — either update the key policy to include the service role (requires KMS IAM change and propagation), or redo the rotation under a documented runbook that grants access BEFORE switching alias.

taylor: I'll coordinate with security to update key policy. creating a quick IAM change: add principal arn:aws:iam::123456789:role/service-role with kms:Decrypt on the key resource. after that, we can re-run rotation in a canary and confirm.

jen: customer impact note: some premium customers saw transient 502s for ~8 minutes during canary window. support notified and triage note created in Zendesk: ZD-19283.

rohan: handing off to night oncall @taylor for monitoring and follow-up. summary: root cause - rotation job created new key or aliased key without granting decrypt to service role. short-term mitigation - feature flag kill + env fallback; long-term - update runbook to ensure key policy grants and atomic alias swap with grace period.

taylor: acknowledged. I'll keep monitoring and will reopen if errors spike above 1%. assigning postmortem to rohan and alex for next steps.

incident-bot: Incident INC-20260315-047 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Owner: rohan. Postmortem scheduled: 2026-03-16 15:00 UTC.

alex: note to add to release checklist: verify KMS key policy grants and run key-policy-validation script as preflight. snippet: 
```
# preflight
aws kms get-key-policy --key-id $NEW_KEY_ID --policy | jq '.Statement[] | select(.Principal.AWS|contains("service-role"))'
```

sam: closing comments: good rapid response. we'll treat this as release-process gap, not code bug. will draft postmortem with timeline and remediation actions. :thumbsup:
